More exciting news from @OpenAI: GPT-Image-2.5-Sunburst is #1 and Flare is #2 across the Text-to-Image Arena, the Image Edit Arena, and the Multi-Image Edit Arena!

Both releases are significant improvements over GPT-Image-2 (medium) in all 3 Arenas. Sunburst delivers the highest quality generation, while Flare still improves upon GPT Image 2 at significantly faster speeds.

The increase by points are (Sunburst | Flare):
- Text-to-Image: +40 | +18 pts
- Single-Image Edit: +59 | +30 pts
- Multi-Image Edit: +81 | +47 pts

Across all categories like 3D Imaging & Modeling, Art and more, Sunburst is #1 and Flare holds #2 in all three Arenas.

Congrats to the team at @OpenAI!
ChatGPT Images 2.5 — another step for creating whatever you can dream of.

Meet GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and Sunburst.

Introducing new image models in the API, with sharper detail, stronger style adherence, and more control over edits.

Agent Arena results for GPT-6 Astra (Max) by @OpenAI are in: it debuts at #2 overall with +12.5% net improvement across +8.9K real-world agentic sessions!

GPT-6 Astra (Max) scored a massive +40.6% in Praise vs. Complaint (implicit sentiment in user reactions), and +21.9% in Confirmed Success (explicit user feedback that the task worked).

With a $4.01 cost per median task, it also reshapes the Pareto frontier for Agent Arena. More info on Astra’s performance compared to cost below.

Congrats to @OpenAI on this release!
One of the most amazing moments for me in OpenAI history was watching this happen over the past week:

We’re sharing a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, one of the deepest problems at the frontier of mathematics.

The proof was produced by a group of agents, using an OpenAI next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra.

The problem concerns whether the description of smooth three-dimensional fluid motion modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations can break down. It has remained unresolved for roughly 90 years.
ChatGPT-6 Astra composes a complete fugue in the style of Bach -- in a single prompt. This is the most impressive musical feat I’ve ever seen from an LLM.
